The doctor behind the white coat

A shoulder surgeon who treats the person, not just the scan.

Shoulder pain has a way of quietly shrinking your life — the shelf you stop reaching for, the side you can't sleep on, the sport you give up. Dr. Bheeshma's focus is the opposite: restoring the full, confident movement you had before, using the least invasive approach that will hold.

Beyond the operating theatre, he's known for making medicine relatable — sharing surgical learning, recovery insight and honest doctor life with a growing community. That same clarity comes into the consult room: you'll always understand what's happening in your shoulder and why a given treatment is right for you.

Conditions treated

Shoulder problems, understood clearly.

If your shoulder hurts at night, feels weak, catches or won't move the way it should, it's worth an expert opinion. These are the conditions seen most often.

01

Rotator cuff tears

Weakness, night pain and trouble lifting the arm — from partial tears to full-thickness ruptures.

02

Frozen shoulder

Adhesive capsulitis — a stiff, painful shoulder that slowly loses its range of motion.

03

Instability & dislocation

Shoulders that slip, feel loose, or repeatedly dislocate after a first injury.

04

Labral & SLAP tears

Deep catching or clicking from tears of the cartilage rim that stabilises the joint.

05

Shoulder arthritis

Grinding, aching and lost movement as the joint surface wears down over time.

06

AC joint injuries

Pain and swelling over the top of the shoulder after a fall or contact injury.

07

Sports & overuse

Throwing, swimming and gym injuries that need a proper return-to-play plan.

08

Fractures

Breaks around the shoulder and upper arm needing precise repair and rehab.

Treatments & procedures

The right fix — not always surgery.

Most shoulders improve without an operation. When surgery is the answer, keyhole technique means smaller scars, less pain and a faster return to normal life.

A1

Shoulder arthroscopy (keyhole)

Diagnosis and repair through small incisions with a camera — the foundation of modern shoulder surgery.

A2

Rotator cuff repair

Reattaching torn tendons to bone to restore strength and end night pain.

A3

Shoulder stabilisation

Bankart and Latarjet procedures to stop a shoulder that keeps dislocating.

A4

Shoulder replacement

Anatomic and reverse arthroplasty for advanced arthritis and complex cuff damage.

A5

Frozen shoulder release

Guided physiotherapy, injections and, when needed, arthroscopic release of the tight capsule.

A6

Non-surgical & injection therapy

Targeted rehab, image-guided injections and pain management to avoid surgery where possible.

Common questions

Before you book.

If shoulder pain lasts more than a couple of weeks, wakes you at night, causes weakness, or your shoulder catches, clicks or feels unstable, it's worth an expert assessment rather than waiting it out.

No. Most shoulder problems improve with the right rehabilitation, activity changes and targeted injections. Surgery is only recommended when it's genuinely the best route to lasting recovery — and that decision is always made with you.

Keyhole surgery using a small camera and instruments through tiny incisions. It allows precise repair with less tissue damage, smaller scars, less pain and a faster recovery than traditional open surgery.

It varies with the tear, but most people wear a sling for a few weeks, then progress through guided physiotherapy over several months. You'll get a clear, stage-by-stage recovery plan tailored to your shoulder.
